title: Why does the Qur'an say woe to those who pray?

beats.narration: There's a verse that says: woe to those who pray. Yes — to those who pray. Why?
The chapter had been describing someone who denies the Judgment: he shoves the orphan away, won't feed the poor. Then the verdict lands — not on him. So ruin is for those who perform the prayer.
The same word, musallin, appears elsewhere naming the saved: everyone is in loss — except those who pray. One participle. Rescue there. Ruin here. What changed?
Not whether they pray — how. The next verses answer: inattentive, performing to be seen. Prayer that leaves the orphan shoved has quietly become the very denial it was meant to oppose.
